content: 1. Primidone and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Primidone reduces the levels of amphotericin B deoxycholate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is relevant only when both drugs are administered orally. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 2. Valganciclovir and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Valganciclovir increases the toxicity of amphotericin B deoxycholate through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 3. Zidovudine and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Zidovudine enhances the toxicity of amphotericin B deoxycholate via pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical relevance of this interaction remains uncertain. 4. Acyclovir and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration of acyclovir and amphotericin B deoxycholate increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 5. Adefovir and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 6. Amikacin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: The combination of these drugs significantly increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. This combination is contraindicated. 7. Amobarbital and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amobarbital reduces the levels of amphotericin B deoxycholate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. The clinical significance is unknown. 8. Atracurium and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amphotericin B deoxycholate enhances the effects of atracurium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 9. Beclomethasone (Inhaled) and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Inhaled beclomethasone increases the toxicity of amphotericin B deoxycholate through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 10. Corticosteroids and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Corticosteroids may potentiate the hypokalemic effects of amphotericin B. Close monitoring of potassium levels is advised. 11. Benazepril and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration of these drugs may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of hypotension. Use caution and monitor blood pressure closely. 12. Budesonide and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Budesonide may interact with amphotericin B deoxycholate through an unspecified mechanism, potentially causing hypokalemia. The clinical significance is unknown. 13. Butabarbital and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Butabarbital reduces the levels of amphotericin B deoxycholate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. The clinical significance is unknown. 14. Butalbital and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Butalbital decreases the levels of amphotericin B deoxycholate by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is relevant only for oral administration. The clinical significance is unknown. 15. Capreomycin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration of these drugs increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 16. Captopril and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: These drugs may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, leading to a greater risk of hypotension. Blood pressure should be closely monitored. 17. Carboplatin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: The combination of these drugs increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 18. Cephaloridine and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration of these drugs significantly increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 19. Cidofovir and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: The combination of these drugs is contraindicated due to a high risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. 20. Cisatracurium and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amphotericin B deoxycholate enhances the effects of cisatracurium through pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 21. Cisplatin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration of these drugs increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 22. Colistin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: The combination of these drugs significantly increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 23. Contrast Media (Iodinated) and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration of these agents is contraindicated due to a high risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. 24. Corticotropin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: This combination may lead to hypokalemia through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 25. Cortisone and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Cortisone may interact with amphotericin B deoxycholate through an unspecified mechanism, potentially causing hypokalemia. The clinical significance is unknown. 26. Cosyntropin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: This combination may lead to hypokalemia through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 27. Cyclosporine and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration of these drugs is contraindicated due to a high risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. 28. Deflazacort and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs decrease serum potassium levels. Monitor potassium levels closely. 29. Dexamethasone and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: This combination may lead to hypokalemia through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 30. Dichlorphenamide and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Both drugs decrease serum potassium levels and may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 31. Digoxin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Amphotericin B deoxycholate enhances the effects of digoxin through pharmacodynamic synergism, particularly if hypokalemia occurs. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 32. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration of these drugs increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Flucytosine and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Flucytosine increases the effects of amphotericin B deoxycholate through pharmacodynamic synergism, while amphotericin B deoxycholate increases flucytosine levels by reducing its elimination. The clinical significance is unknown. 34. Fludrocortisone and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: This combination may lead to hypokalemia through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 35. Foscarnet and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration of these drugs increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 36. Ganciclovir and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Ganciclovir increases the toxicity of amphotericin B deoxycholate through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance is unknown. 37. Gentamicin and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration of these drugs significantly increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Avoid this combination or use alternative drugs. 38. Hydrocortisone and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: This combination may lead to hypokalemia through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown. 39. Ifosfamide and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Ifosfamide increases the toxicity of amphotericin B deoxycholate through an unknown mechanism. Monitor for renal toxicity, bronchospasm, and hypotension. 40. Iloprost and Amphotericin B Deoxycholate: Co-administration of these drugs may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored.
